$625Add-on estimate (§6)

4 partsSearch link, catalog page, product page, cart page (§2)

You want to keep about 20,000 items in your main stores, and also let customers search and buy from your suppliers' 100,000+ SKUs. This add-on does that with a separate supplier catalog site, linked from your store search. It covers only the pages a customer needs to find and buy a part, so it costs much less than a full site.

1

How it works for your customers

#What the customer doesWhat they see
1Searches your main store and doesn't find the partA "Search for …" link to the supplier catalog, with their search term already filled in (§2.1)
2Opens the supplier catalogSearch results from the 100,000+ supplier SKUs, with filters (§2.2)
3Clicks a productA product page with pictures, price, stock and description (§2.3)
4Adds it to the cart and checks outA cart page with a discount / free shipping code field, then Shopify checkout (§2.4)

Your 20,000 items stay in your main stores with their own design. The supplier SKUs live on their own site, so they don't fill up your main catalog, search or filters. Supplier orders go through the supplier site's own cart and checkout, separate from the main store.

2

What we build

The screenshots below are from another Shopify store and show the layout we'd follow. We set it up with your logo, colors and products.

2.1 Link from your store search

ReferenceAnother store's search popup. We add a "Search for …" link like this to your main store search. It opens the supplier catalog with the same search term.

2.2 Supplier catalog page

ReferenceAnother store's search results page. Customers search the 100,000+ supplier SKUs here, see the number of results, and narrow them down with "Filter & Sort".

2.3 Product page

ReferenceAnother store's product page. Each supplier part gets the same: pictures, price, stock status, "Add to cart" and tabs for description and shipping.

2.4 Cart page

ReferenceAnother store's cart page. We add a code field on the cart, so customers can enter a discount or free shipping code before checkout.

Why this keeps the cost down

Customers reach the supplier catalog through search, so it doesn't need a homepage or collection pages. That is where most of the design and build time in a normal site goes.

4

Supplier product data

The 25h covers building the pages. Getting the 100,000+ supplier products into the catalog depends on how your suppliers share their data, so we quote it once we know the format (§5).

Import time: Shopify lets a store add about 1,000 new variants per day once it has more than about 50,000. Importing 100,000+ SKUs therefore takes several weeks, so we'd start with the parts most likely to sell.
5

Open questions

#QuestionWhy it matters
1How do your suppliers share their catalogs: CSV/Excel file, API or feed?Sets how we import the products and how it's priced (§4)
2How often do supplier prices and stock change?Decides whether we need an automatic sync
3Do the supplier items come with pictures and descriptions?Product pages (§2.3) need them; without them, pages show basic data only
4Which sites should link to the supplier catalog: all three, or mainly one?Sets where we add the search link (§2.1) and the design it follows
5Which domain would you like for it (for example parts.atv-fritid.se)?We set it up at launch
